title: Shadow appraisal runner: AppraisalInput → LLM → AppraisalOutput
objective: Create a shadow appraisal runner module at back/app/llm/shadow_runner.py that accepts an AppraisalInput, uses LlmAppraisalRequest to render the prompt, calls the Anthropic API offline, parses the raw response via parse_llm_response, and returns an AppraisalOutput. On any ParseError or API error, the runner must fall back to AppraisalOutput.from_deterministic_fallback and record the failure reason. No live engine path is touched.
exact_scope: One new module: back/app/llm/shadow_runner.py containing a ShadowAppraisalRunner class (or equivalent top-level function) with a single public entry point run(input: AppraisalInput) -> ShadowRunResult. One new test file: back/tests/test_p30_t2_shadow_runner.py covering all required tests listed below. No changes to any existing module outside back/app/llm/. No changes to engines, settlement, tick_bridge, or any live simulation path.
constraints: Must not modify back/app/engines/appraisal_settlement.py or any other engine module.
Must not modify back/app/llm/prompt_schema.py or back/app/llm/response_parser.py.
Must not modify back/app/domain/appraisal_output.py — AppraisalOutput schema is frozen.
Must not modify back/app/domain/appraisal_input.py — AppraisalInput schema is frozen.
The runner must never write to any state — it is a pure read-then-return pipeline.
The runner must not be wired into the live tick pipeline (day_simulator, tick_bridge, or any API route).
The LLM call must be the Anthropic API (claude-sonnet-4-6 or equivalent current model). No OpenAI or other provider.
The runner must not use streaming — a single complete response per invocation.

On any failure (ParseError, API error, network error, timeout), the runner must return the deterministic fallback output via AppraisalOutput.from_deterministic_fallback rather than raising to the caller.
fallback_used on the returned AppraisalOutput must accurately reflect whether the LLM path succeeded (False) or the fallback was used (True).
The module must be importable with no side effects — no LLM call happens at import time.
API key must be read from the environment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); the key must not be hardcoded.
Tests must use monkeypatching or a fake/stub transport to simulate LLM responses — no real API calls in the test suite.
acceptance_criteria: A ShadowRunResult model (or dataclass) is defined in shadow_runner.py carrying: output (AppraisalOutput), llm_used (bool indicating whether the LLM path was taken), failure_reason (Optional[str] set when fallback was used), raw_response (Optional[str] the raw text returned by the LLM before parsing).

run(input) with a stubbed LLM that returns a valid JSON response produces a ShadowRunResult where llm_used=True, failure_reason=None, output.fallback_used=False, and output fields match the stubbed response.

run(input) with a stubbed LLM that returns malformed JSON produces a ShadowRunResult where llm_used=False, failure_reason contains a non-empty string, output.fallback_used=True, and output matches AppraisalOutput.from_deterministic_fallback.
run(input) with a stubbed LLM that raises an API-level exception produces a ShadowRunResult where llm_used=False, failure_reason is non-empty, and output.fallback_used=True.
run(input) with a T1 input and a valid stubbed LLM response sets output.tick_type to EventCategory.information_exposure in the returned output.
run(input) with a T2 input (relational_context present) and a valid stubbed response that includes a non-null relational block returns that relational block unmodified in output.relational.
run(input) with a T4 input (social_event_context present) and a valid stubbed response is handled without error.
The prompt sent to the LLM is the same string that LlmAppraisalRequest.from_appraisal_input produces for the same input — the runner must not construct prompts independently.
The runner is importable with no environment variable set and no network call occurring at import time.
All existing tests (back/tests/) continue to pass without modification.
required_tests: When the LLM returns a valid surface-absorption neutral T1 response, the runner returns a result with llm_used=True and output.absorption equal to surface.
When the LLM returns unparseable text (not JSON), the runner returns a result with llm_used=False, a non-empty failure_reason, and output.fallback_used=True.
When the LLM call raises an exception (simulated API error), the runner returns a result with llm_used=False and output.fallback_used=True rather than propagating the exception.
The raw_response field on a successful LLM run contains the exact text that the LLM returned before parsing.
The raw_response field on a failed parse attempt contains the text that was returned but failed to parse.
The raw_response field is None when the LLM call itself raised an exception (no text was returned).
For a T1 input, the prompt text passed to the LLM contains the headline and trending_topic from the input's world_context.
For a T2 input, the prompt text passed to the LLM contains the target_name from the input's relational_context.
The runner never calls AppraisalOutput.from_deterministic_fallback when the LLM path succeeds and the response is valid.
When a valid LLM response contains absorption=deep with a growth list of two dimensions, the returned output carries all growth entries intact.
non_goals: Wiring the shadow runner into any live API route or tick pipeline.
Adding retry logic or exponential backoff for the LLM call.
Supporting any LLM provider other than Anthropic.
Adding a CLI or management interface for invoking the runner.
Logging or persisting run results to disk or any external store.
Modifying the deterministic fallback behavior or any settlement logic.
Adding confidence thresholds or gating settlement on runner output.
Supporting batch or parallel invocations in this task.
